"""Create artifact-tool workspaces for editable PPTX export from deck specs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from presentation_agent.html_deck import DeckSpecError, catalog_ids, load_json, validate_deck_spec


JsonMap = dict[str, Any]

DEFAULT_SLIDE_SIZE = "1280x720"


def create_artifact_workspace(
    spec_path: str | Path,
    workspace_path: str | Path,
    *,
    catalog_path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Write artifact-tool slide modules and source notes for a deck spec."""

    spec = load_json(spec_path)
    known_ids = catalog_ids(load_json(catalog_path)) if catalog_path else None
    gaps = validate_deck_spec(spec, known_reference_ids=known_ids)
    if gaps:
        raise DeckSpecError("; ".join(gaps))

    workspace = Path(workspace_path)
    slides_dir = workspace / "slides"
    preview_dir = workspace / "preview"
    layout_dir = workspace / "layout"
    output_dir = workspace / "output"
    qa_dir = workspace / "qa"
    for directory in (slides_dir, preview_dir, layout_dir, output_dir, qa_dir):
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    spec_copy_path = workspace / "deck-spec.json"
    spec_copy_path.write_text(json.dumps(spec, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    slides = spec["slides"]
    for index, slide in enumerate(slides, start=1):
        module_path = slides_dir / f"slide-{index:02d}.mjs"
        module_path.write_text(_render_slide_module(index, slide, spec), encoding="utf-8")

    source_notes_path = workspace / "source-notes.md"
    source_notes_path.write_text(_render_source_notes(spec), encoding="utf-8")

    manifest = {
        "schema_version": "2026-06-01",
        "purpose": "artifact-tool workspace generated from presentation-agent deck-spec",
        "deck_title": spec["title"],
        "slide_count": len(slides),
        "workspace": str(workspace),
        "slides_dir": str(slides_dir),
        "preview_dir": str(preview_dir),
        "layout_dir": str(layout_dir),
        "output_dir": str(output_dir),
        "source_notes": str(source_notes_path),
        "final_pptx": str(output_dir / _slug(spec["title"], suffix=".pptx")),
        "builder_command_template": (
            "node $PRESENTATIONS_SKILL_DIR/scripts/build_artifact_deck.mjs "
            "--slides-dir {slides_dir} --preview-dir {preview_dir} --layout-dir {layout_dir} "
            "--out {final_pptx} --manifest {manifest_path} --slide-count {slide_count} --slide-size 1280x720"
        ),
    }
    manifest_path = workspace / "artifact-workspace-manifest.json"
    manifest["builder_command"] = manifest["builder_command_template"].format(
        slides_dir=slides_dir,
        preview_dir=preview_dir,
        layout_dir=layout_dir,
        final_pptx=manifest["final_pptx"],
        manifest_path=workspace / "artifact-build-manifest.json",
        slide_count=len(slides),
    )
    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return manifest


def _render_slide_module(index: int, slide: JsonMap, spec: JsonMap) -> str:
    palette = spec.get("theme", {}).get("palette", {})
    colors = {
        "background": palette.get("background", "#f6f4ef"),
        "surface": palette.get("surface", "#ffffff"),
        "ink": palette.get("ink", "#202124"),
        "muted": palette.get("muted", "#62605a"),
        "accent": palette.get("accent", "#0f766e"),
        "warm": palette.get("warm", "#c2410c"),
        "cool": palette.get("cool", "#2563eb"),
        "line": palette.get("line", "#d8d5cc"),
    }
    layout = slide.get("layout", "split")
    title = _js(slide.get("title", ""))
    kicker = _js(slide.get("kicker", ""))
    subtitle = _js(slide.get("subtitle", ""))
    body = slide.get("body", [])
    body_items = body if isinstance(body, list) else [body]
    notes = slide.get("speaker_notes", [])
    visual = slide.get("visual", {}) if isinstance(slide.get("visual"), dict) else {}
    evidence = slide.get("evidence_sources", [])

    lines = [
        f"export async function slide{index:02d}(presentation, ctx) {{",
        "  const slide = presentation.slides.add();",
        f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 0, y: 0, w: 1280, h: 720, fill: {_js(colors['surface'])}, line: ctx.line('transparent', 0) }});",
        f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 0, y: 0, w: 1280, h: 18, fill: {_js(colors['accent'])}, line: ctx.line('transparent', 0) }});",
    ]

    if layout in {"hero", "closing"}:
        lines.extend(
            [
                f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {kicker}, x: 72, y: 94, w: 520, h: 34, fontSize: 17, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['accent'])} }});",
                f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {title}, x: 72, y: 160, w: 760, h: 210, fontSize: 66, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['ink'])}, insets: {{ left: 0, right: 0, top: 0, bottom: 0 }} }});",
                f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {subtitle}, x: 76, y: 414, w: 780, h: 96, fontSize: 24, color: {_js(colors['muted'])}, insets: {{ left: 0, right: 0, top: 0, bottom: 0 }} }});",
                f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 914, y: 126, w: 250, h: 250, geometry: 'ellipse', fill: {_js(colors['background'])}, line: ctx.line({_js(colors['line'])}, 2) }});",
                f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(slide.get('script_beat', ''))}, x: 926, y: 230, w: 226, h: 48, fontSize: 22, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['warm'])}, align: 'center', valign: 'mid' }});",
            ]
        )
    else:
        lines.extend(
            [
                f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {kicker}, x: 62, y: 58, w: 520, h: 30, fontSize: 15, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['accent'])} }});",
                f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {title}, x: 62, y: 104, w: 560, h: 126, fontSize: 42, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['ink'])} }});",
            ]
        )
        y = 270
        for item in body_items[:4]:
            lines.extend(
                [
                    f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 66, y: {y + 8}, w: 5, h: 42, fill: {_js(colors['accent'])}, line: ctx.line('transparent', 0) }});",
                    f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(item)}, x: 88, y: {y}, w: 520, h: 58, fontSize: 22, color: {_js(colors['ink'])} }});",
                ]
            )
            y += 74
        lines.extend(_render_visual_js(visual, colors))

    lines.extend(_render_footer_js(slide, evidence, colors))
    lines.extend(_render_speaker_notes_js(notes, colors))
    lines.append("  return slide;")
    lines.append("}\n")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _render_visual_js(visual: JsonMap, colors: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    visual_type = visual.get("type", "statement")
    if visual_type == "metric":
        return [
            f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 735, y: 146, w: 360, h: 360, geometry: 'ellipse', fill: {_js(colors['background'])}, line: ctx.line({_js(colors['line'])}, 2) }});",
            f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(visual.get('value', ''))}, x: 760, y: 240, w: 310, h: 112, fontSize: 92, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['warm'])}, align: 'center', valign: 'mid' }});",
            f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(visual.get('label', ''))}, x: 772, y: 368, w: 286, h: 76, fontSize: 20, color: {_js(colors['muted'])}, align: 'center', valign: 'mid' }});",
        ]
    if visual_type == "steps":
        lines = [
            f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 710, y: 150, w: 410, h: 420, fill: {_js(colors['background'])}, line: ctx.line({_js(colors['line'])}, 2) }});",
        ]
        for index, step in enumerate(visual.get("steps", [])[:5], start=1):
            y = 182 + (index - 1) * 68
            lines.extend(
                [
                    f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 744, y: {y}, w: 44, h: 44, geometry: 'ellipse', fill: {_js(colors['cool'])}, line: ctx.line('transparent', 0) }});",
                    f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(index)}, x: 744, y: {y + 7}, w: 44, h: 28, fontSize: 16, bold: true, color: '#ffffff', align: 'center', valign: 'mid' }});",
                    f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(step)}, x: 810, y: {y + 2}, w: 250, h: 42, fontSize: 22, color: {_js(colors['ink'])} }});",
                ]
            )
        return lines
    if visual_type == "cards":
        lines = []
        for index, card in enumerate(visual.get("cards", [])[:3]):
            if not isinstance(card, dict):
                continue
            y = 150 + index * 132
            lines.extend(
                [
                    f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 700, y: {y}, w: 420, h: 104, fill: {_js(colors['background'])}, line: ctx.line({_js(colors['line'])}, 2) }});",
                    f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(card.get('title', ''))}, x: 728, y: {y + 20}, w: 360, h: 26, fontSize: 21, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['ink'])} }});",
                    f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(card.get('text', ''))}, x: 728, y: {y + 54}, w: 360, h: 30, fontSize: 16, color: {_js(colors['muted'])} }});",
                ]
            )
        return lines
    return [
        f"  ctx.addShape(slide, {{ x: 718, y: 170, w: 382, h: 310, fill: {_js(colors['background'])}, line: ctx.line({_js(colors['line'])}, 2) }});",
        f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(visual.get('label', ''))}, x: 756, y: 286, w: 306, h: 82, fontSize: 26, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['warm'])}, align: 'center', valign: 'mid' }});",
    ]


def _render_footer_js(slide: JsonMap, evidence: Any, colors: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    source_text = "Sources: " + ", ".join(str(item) for item in evidence) if isinstance(evidence, list) and evidence else ""
    return [
        f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(source_text)}, x: 62, y: 666, w: 940, h: 26, fontSize: 10, color: {_js(colors['muted'])} }});",
        f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js(slide.get('script_beat', ''))}, x: 1052, y: 660, w: 150, h: 28, fontSize: 11, bold: true, color: {_js(colors['accent'])}, align: 'right' }});",
    ]


def _render_speaker_notes_js(notes: Any, colors: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    if not isinstance(notes, list) or not notes:
        return []
    joined = " / ".join(str(note) for note in notes)
    return [
        f"  ctx.addText(slide, {{ text: {_js('Speaker notes: ' + joined)}, x: 62, y: 620, w: 1040, h: 28, fontSize: 9, color: {_js(colors['muted'])} }});",
    ]


def _render_source_notes(spec: JsonMap) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"# Source Notes: {spec['title']}",
        "",
        "## Reference Sources",
        "",
    ]
    for source_id in spec.get("reference_sources", []):
        lines.append(f"- `{source_id}`")
    lines.extend(["", "## Speaker Notes", ""])
    for slide in spec.get("slides", []):
        lines.append(f"### {slide.get('id', '')}: {slide.get('title', '')}")
        for note in slide.get("speaker_notes", []):
            lines.append(f"- {note}")
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _slug(value: str, *, suffix: str = "") -> str:
    raw = "".join(char.lower() if char.isalnum() else "-" for char in value)
    collapsed = "-".join(part for part in raw.split("-") if part)
    return f"{collapsed[:80] or 'presentation'}{suffix}"


def _js(value: Any) -> str:
    return json.dumps(str(value), ensure_ascii=False)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Create an artifact-tool PPTX workspace from a deck spec.")
    parser.add_argument("deck_spec", help="Path to deck spec JSON")
    parser.add_argument("workspace", help="Output artifact-tool workspace")
    parser.add_argument("--catalog", help="Optional reference catalog for source ID validation")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        manifest = create_artifact_workspace(args.deck_spec, args.workspace, catalog_path=args.catalog)
    except DeckSpecError as error:
        print(f"ERROR: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Validate and summarize presentation reference catalogs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import urlparse


REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS = {
    "schema_version",
    "reader_guide",
    "reference_links",
    "structure_rules",
    "field_guide",
    "records",
}

REQUIRED_RECORD_FIELDS = {
    "id",
    "title",
    "url",
    "source_type",
    "formats",
    "license_status",
    "download_allowed",
    "html_conversion",
    "design_tags",
    "quality_signals",
    "provenance",
    "notes",
}

ALLOWED_LICENSE_STATUSES = {
    "open_source",
    "public_domain",
    "free_with_terms",
    "permissive_possible",
    "official_terms_required",
    "paid_or_account_required",
    "unknown",
}

RAW_STORAGE_COMPATIBLE = {
    "open_source",
    "public_domain",
    "free_with_terms",
    "permissive_possible",
}

ALLOWED_HTML_CONVERSIONS = {
    "native_html",
    "pptx_requires_conversion",
    "manual_rebuild_recommended",
    "reference_only",
    "asset_reference",
}


class CatalogError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a catalog contract is violated."""


def load_catalog(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Load a JSON presentation reference catalog."""

    catalog_path = Path(path)
    with catalog_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        data = json.load(handle)
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise CatalogError("Catalog root must be an object.")
    return data


def validate_catalog(data: dict[str, Any], *, min_records: int = 1) -> list[str]:
    """Return validation gaps for a catalog."""

    gaps: list[str] = []
    missing_top = sorted(REQUIRED_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS - data.keys())
    if missing_top:
        gaps.append(f"Missing top-level fields: {', '.join(missing_top)}")

    records = data.get("records")
    if not isinstance(records, list):
        return gaps + ["records must be a list."]
    if len(records) < min_records:
        gaps.append(f"records must contain at least {min_records} entries.")

    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    for index, record in enumerate(records):
        prefix = f"records[{index}]"
        if not isinstance(record, dict):
            gaps.append(f"{prefix} must be an object.")
            continue

        missing_record = sorted(REQUIRED_RECORD_FIELDS - record.keys())
        if missing_record:
            gaps.append(f"{prefix} missing fields: {', '.join(missing_record)}")

        record_id = record.get("id")
        if not isinstance(record_id, str) or not record_id:
            gaps.append(f"{prefix}.id must be a non-empty string.")
        elif record_id in seen_ids:
            gaps.append(f"Duplicate record id: {record_id}")
        else:
            seen_ids.add(record_id)

        url = record.get("url")
        if not isinstance(url, str) or urlparse(url).scheme not in {"http", "https"}:
            gaps.append(f"{prefix}.url must be an http(s) URL.")

        license_status = record.get("license_status")
        if license_status not in ALLOWED_LICENSE_STATUSES:
            gaps.append(f"{prefix}.license_status is not recognized: {license_status!r}")

        if record.get("download_allowed") is True and license_status not in RAW_STORAGE_COMPATIBLE:
            gaps.append(f"{prefix}.download_allowed=true is not compatible with {license_status!r}.")

        html_conversion = record.get("html_conversion")
        if html_conversion not in ALLOWED_HTML_CONVERSIONS:
            gaps.append(f"{prefix}.html_conversion is not recognized: {html_conversion!r}")

        for list_field in ("formats", "design_tags", "quality_signals"):
            value = record.get(list_field)
            if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
                gaps.append(f"{prefix}.{list_field} must be a non-empty list.")

        provenance = record.get("provenance")
        if not isinstance(provenance, dict):
            gaps.append(f"{prefix}.provenance must be an object.")
        else:
            if not provenance.get("accessed_on"):
                gaps.append(f"{prefix}.provenance.accessed_on is required.")
            if not provenance.get("found_via"):
                gaps.append(f"{prefix}.provenance.found_via is required.")

    return gaps


def summarize_catalog(data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarize catalog coverage for quick review."""

    records = data.get("records", [])
    return {
        "record_count": len(records),
        "source_types": dict(Counter(record["source_type"] for record in records)),
        "license_statuses": dict(Counter(record["license_status"] for record in records)),
        "html_conversions": dict(Counter(record["html_conversion"] for record in records)),
        "download_allowed_count": sum(1 for record in records if record.get("download_allowed")),
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = argv if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:]
    if not args:
        print("Usage: python -m presentation_agent.catalog <catalog.json>", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    data = load_catalog(args[0])
    gaps = validate_catalog(data, min_records=40)
    if gaps:
        for gap in gaps:
            print(f"ERROR: {gap}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print(json.dumps(summarize_catalog(data), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from presentation_agent.html_deck import build_html_deck, catalog_ids, load_json, render_deck, validate_deck_spec


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CATALOG_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "reference-index" / "starter-reference-catalog.json"
SPEC_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "deck-specs" / "presentation-agent-kickoff.ko.json"


class HtmlDeckTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_sample_deck_spec_is_valid_against_catalog(self) -> None:
        catalog = load_json(CATALOG_PATH)
        spec = load_json(SPEC_PATH)

        gaps = validate_deck_spec(spec, known_reference_ids=catalog_ids(catalog))

        self.assertEqual([], gaps)

        spec = load_json(SPEC_PATH)

        rendered = render_deck(spec)

        self.assertEqual(6, rendered.count("<section class=\"pa-slide"))

        rendered = render_deck(spec)

        for line in rendered.splitlines():

patterns.label: Permissioned Tool Execution
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: Settings and permissions have scopes and precedence, while CLAUDE.md-style instructions are contextual guidance rather than hard enforcement.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Separate behavioral guidance from enforced execution policy.
patterns.platformMapping: Keep CLI adapters optional, use allowlisted Tauri commands, persist human decisions, and route unsafe source-affecting choices through the decision inbox.
implementationTargets: Show permission and source-boundary status in Workspace Monitor
Add per-adapter permission summaries before source-affecting task pipes
riskControls: no global CLI install without audit
explicit human checkpoint for destructive operations

patterns.label: Plan Before Edit
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: Plan mode reads files and proposes a plan before disk edits for changes that need review.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Use reversible planning gates before durable source or policy edits.
patterns.platformMapping: Map plan mode to work modes, spec-driven tasks, task pipe merge gates, and decision inbox checkpoints.
implementationTargets: Add a first-class Plan Gate indicator to Desktop task pipes
Show blocked decisions next to the source editor before Save All
riskControls: mode selection record for non-quick work

patterns.label: Durable Instruction Memory
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: CLAUDE.md and auto memory are loaded into sessions, but enforcement belongs in settings or hooks.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Keep shared durable instructions thin, traceable, and separate from hard policy.
patterns.platformMapping: Use AGENTS.md as a runtime adapter entrypoint and keep durable policy in shared docs/configs with memory bootstrap anchors.
implementationTargets: Show memory bootstrap hot anchors in Workspace Monitor
Flag adapter instructions that duplicate durable policy
riskControls: do not fork durable policy across adapters
specific concise instructions over vague preferences

patterns.label: Subagent Context Isolation
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: Subagents preserve main context by handling side tasks in separate contexts with scoped tool access.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Treat exploration, research, validation, implementation, and merge gates as separate lanes with explicit summaries.
patterns.platformMapping: Expose agent collaboration lanes, task pipe presets, blockers, and merge gates rather than dumping every log into the main task view.
implementationTargets: Add per-lane context budget and summary contracts
Surface lane handoff quality in Unified Ops
riskControls: parallel lanes need non-overlapping touch paths

patterns.label: MCP Connector Boundary
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: MCP connects external tools and data sources, but trust and prompt-injection risks must be reviewed before connecting servers.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Connectors are optional capability cards with trust, scope, and lifecycle checks.
patterns.platformMapping: Keep MCP-style connectors behind capability setup, permission review, and source-boundary warnings rather than making them required platform runtime dependencies.
implementationTargets: Add connector cards next to CLI adapter cards
Record connector trust decisions in the decision inbox

patterns.label: Hook Event Automation
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: Hooks can run commands around tool and session events, and command hooks run with the user's permissions.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Automation hooks need explicit event schemas, allowlists, rollback, and resource guards.
patterns.platformMapping: Use hook-like workflows only after modeling event input/output, cleanup, and user permission impact.
implementationTargets: Create a platform hook registry with disabled-by-default executable hooks

patterns.label: Skill On-Demand Packaging
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: Skills package repeatable workflows and load detailed instructions only when relevant.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Promote repeated work into the smallest durable capability before adding product code.
patterns.platformMapping: Use templates, tools, skills, prompts, workflows, and agents as staged capability assets; surface promotion candidates in evidence/promotion views.
implementationTargets: Show skill candidates from work history bottlenecks

riskControls: forward-test before relying on a skill

patterns.label: Parallel Worktree Sessions
patterns.claudeCodeSignal: Parallel sessions can run in separate worktrees to reduce edit collisions.
patterns.transferPrinciple: Parallel execution requires branch/worktree isolation or explicit touch-path locks.
patterns.platformMapping: Task pipes should record lane touch paths, dependencies, and merge strategy before launching overlapping implementation work.
implementationTargets: Add worktree-aware task pipe launch options

productPosition.productClaim: A desktop platform whose core is Agent Core for easy custom agent and subagent creation plus CLI orchestration for continuous Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, OpenCode, and other guest CLI work with deferred decisions and task-run records. Root tools, workspace workbench, learning, and observability support those two core capabilities.

desktopHomeSurface.homeCopyRule: The first screen shall emphasize Agent Core, CLI orchestration continuity, Tool Studio for shared root tools, and at-a-glance work visibility before workbench, learning, or observability details.
desktopHomeSurface.configurationRule: Core setup for provider accounts, CLI adapters, root tools, workspace access, and question deferral shall be visible from Home and collected in the execution settings surface.

referenceLinks.title: Visual Studio Code user interface
referenceLinks.limitation: UI structure is documented, not a direct product strategy document.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use one activity rail, a focused side bar, an editor center, and a bottom panel for terminal/output.

referenceLinks.title: IntelliJ Platform UI overview
referenceLinks.limitation: Plugin SDK docs describe default workbench areas rather than AI workflows.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use tool windows around the editor and avoid duplicate sidebars that compete for navigation.

referenceLinks.title: IntelliJ IDEA tool windows
referenceLinks.limitation: Tool-window documentation is IDE-general and must be translated into agent run semantics.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Put Run Configuration, Services, Problems, and status context at the top of the Desktop Runtime surface so execution, setup gaps, and blockers are visible before long panels.

referenceLinks.title: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
referenceLinks.limitation: Cloud GitHub-centered flow differs from local desktop ownership.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Model task intake as research, plan, branch/workspace changes, validation, diff review, and PR/commit handoff.

referenceLinks.title: GitHub Copilot cloud agent risks and mitigations
referenceLinks.limitation: GitHub-specific controls need local equivalents.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Keep tool access, untrusted input, automation approval, and workflow approval visible in the platform.

referenceLinks.title: Claude Code overview
referenceLinks.limitation: Product claims should be translated into platform-neutral patterns.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Support terminal, desktop, IDE-like diff review, multiple sessions, scheduled tasks, MCP, hooks, skills, and agent teams as replaceable capability lanes.

referenceLinks.title: Claude Code custom subagents
referenceLinks.limitation: Subagent details are Claude-specific.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Agent Core must create specialized workers with separate context, explicit tools, permissions, memory, and resume behavior.

referenceLinks.title: Claude Code hooks
referenceLinks.limitation: Hook event names differ across tools.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Add platform-level pre-tool, permission, post-tool, failure, stop, and elicitation gates.

referenceLinks.title: Claude Code MCP
referenceLinks.limitation: MCP examples are Claude-specific but the protocol and trust concerns generalize.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Surface MCP servers as scoped tool connectors with trust review, auth state, resource references, and elicitation dialogs.

referenceLinks.title: OpenHands key features
referenceLinks.limitation: OpenHands is a full agent system, not only a desktop shell.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Expose chat, changes, embedded editor, terminal, app preview, and browser lanes as separate workbench tabs.

referenceLinks.title: OpenHands Software Agent SDK
referenceLinks.limitation: SDK adoption would need license, dependency, and sandbox review before bundling.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Treat software-agent infrastructure as modular engine candidates instead of hand-rolling every future agent capability.

referenceLinks.title: Cline overview
referenceLinks.limitation: Cline is editor-extension-first.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Keep every file, command, browser, and tool action visible with explicit approval and checkpoint recovery.

referenceLinks.title: Devin Desktop Cascade memories and rules
referenceLinks.limitation: Devin/Windsurf product naming changed; use pattern, not brand-specific file paths.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Separate auto memories, explicit rules, manual workflows, and richer skills so users know what each setting does.

referenceLinks.title: Cursor agent overview
referenceLinks.limitation: The public page redirected during direct fetch; search cache was used for content confirmation.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use sidepane agent, diff review, chat tabs, checkpoints, terminal integration, history, and rules as feature checks.

referenceLinks.title: Cursor background agents
referenceLinks.limitation: The public page redirected during direct fetch; search cache was used for content confirmation.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use asynchronous task agents, remote/isolated machine setup, branch handoff, terminal startup commands, and takeover affordances.

referenceLinks.title: Continue AI pull request checks
referenceLinks.limitation: Current Continue docs emphasize PR checks rather than a full local workbench.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Convert quality rules into markdown checks that can become validation gates and failure-to-fix suggestions.

referenceLinks.title: Aider documentation
referenceLinks.limitation: Terminal-first UX needs desktop wrapping for non-CLI users.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Keep git-native local editing, repo maps, lint/test loops, and scriptability available through guest CLI lanes.

referenceLinks.title: OpenCode docs
referenceLinks.limitation: Terminal-first assumptions need native workbench controls.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use project initialization, AGENTS.md generation, @ file search, plan/build mode split, and multi-provider config patterns.

referenceLinks.title: Hawardshin/claw-code
referenceLinks.limitation: Direct clone returned 403 disabled during this work, and no license file was verified. Public GitHub page plus raw README/CLAW/PARITY documents were reachable, so only architecture and product patterns are transferred.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Add Claw Code as an optional CLI guest adapter and transfer slash-command orchestration, skills/MCP/runtime manifest, hook/plugin gap tracking, and parity-audit patterns without copying source.

referenceLinks.title: Tauri sidecar binaries
referenceLinks.limitation: Sidecars need platform-specific binaries and explicit capabilities.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Bundle local engines as sidecars only with clear permissions, args, runtime contracts, and rollback.

referenceLinks.title: Tauri distribution and signing
referenceLinks.limitation: Public release still needs signing/notarization credentials.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Keep internal test app, customer bundle, public release, signing, notarization, and updater gates distinct.

referenceLinks.title: OWASP LLM01 prompt injection
referenceLinks.limitation: Mitigations reduce risk but do not prove safety.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Treat external content and connected tools as untrusted, enforce least privilege, structured validation, and human approval for high-risk actions.

referenceLinks.title: MCP security best practices
referenceLinks.limitation: MCP security guidance must be combined with local OS and credential boundaries.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use scoped MCP servers, consent boundaries, token handling, local server compromise controls, and tool search to reduce context and risk.

referenceLinks.title: Docker Desktop docs
referenceLinks.limitation: Container management differs from AI agent orchestration.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use one-click install, centralized dashboard, settings, troubleshooting, integrated terminal, extensions, notifications, and resource visibility as native-app patterns.

referenceLinks.title: GitHub Desktop docs
referenceLinks.limitation: GitHub Desktop does not solve AI orchestration itself.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use visual confirmation of changes, branch workflows, commit attribution, push/pull, clone, and PR creation as the Git workbench baseline.

referenceLinks.title: Raycast extensions manual
referenceLinks.limitation: Launcher UX is a support pattern, not the full product shell.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use command palette, extension store, tool selection, background updates, and fast keyboard-first actions for capability launch.

referenceLinks.title: Codex app features
referenceLinks.limitation: Codex app features are OpenAI-specific; transfer only the desktop workbench pattern, not product identity or proprietary UI.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use thread-level workspaces, Local/Worktree/Cloud mode choices, built-in Git/diff, integrated terminal, in-app browser, artifact preview, automations, skills, MCP, and approval/sandbox controls as desktop-agent reference requirements.

referenceLinks.title: Codex app commands
referenceLinks.limitation: Keyboard shortcuts and deep links must be adapted to this platform's naming and native shell.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use command menu, settings shortcut, open-folder action, sidebar/diff/terminal toggles, thread search, find-in-thread, slash commands, and deep links as a desktop interaction baseline.

referenceLinks.title: Codex agent skills
referenceLinks.limitation: Skill discovery and metadata should be platform-neutral and should not assume only Codex can run reusable workflows.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use progressive disclosure, explicit invocation, repository/user/admin/system scopes, plugin packaging, UI metadata, and dependency declarations for Agent Core and capability promotion.

referenceLinks.title: Claude Desktop local MCP servers and desktop extensions
referenceLinks.limitation: MCP in Claude Desktop is documented as beta and uses Claude-specific extension packaging and settings labels.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Use one-click local tool extension installation, Settings > Extensions organization, connector status from the chat composer, manifest-based packaging, sensitive config encryption, debug logs, and enterprise allowlist controls as connector UX requirements.

referenceLinks.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Documentation
referenceLinks.limitation: AWS managed-service details are optional deployment adapters in this product, not mandatory local runtime dependencies or the default execution host.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Expose AgentCore-style lifecycle and capability blueprints in the Agents surface while preserving the desktop app and local Python runtime as the primary host runtime.

referenceLinks.title: awslabs/agentcore-samples
referenceLinks.limitation: Repository is sampled as a public reference; source code is not copied into the product bundle.
referenceLinks.planImpact: Transfer create/local-dev/optional-deploy/invoke, add memory/identity/evaluator/gateway, blueprints, and observability/evaluation as desktop product blueprint controls.

transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 검색 에이전트 실행, CLI 세션, 다중 파이프, 준비 점검을 한 화면의 IDE식 실행 영역에서 바로 시작하고 막힌 이유를 즉시 본다.
implementationTargets: Run Configuration cards call real search agent, CLI session, task pipe, and readiness actions
Services list shows runtime, workspace, adapters, providers, and active sessions
Problems strip links blockers to terminal, settings, questions, or readiness checks
status bar summarizes runtime, CLI, model, sessions, inbox, and terminal state
riskControls: readiness script requires the new workbench tokens
responsive CSS keeps the tool-window layout usable on smaller screens
button actions reuse existing runtime functions instead of mock interactions

transferPatterns.observedStrength: The Codex app treats each task as a desktop thread with project scope, command menu, slash commands, terminal, Git/diff, worktree mode, artifacts, skills, MCP, browser, and approval controls around one work unit.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Treat each agent run chat as a first-class workbench thread: the composer starts work, the bottom panel owns terminal output, the side/inspector area shows files, diff, artifacts, decisions, validations, and a mode selector keeps Local/Worktree/Cloud-like execution explicit.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 검색 에이전트나 다른 에이전트를 실행할 때 채팅, 파일, 터미널, 변경사항, 검증, 기록이 같은 작업 단위로 묶인다는 것을 바로 이해한다.
implementationTargets: every runnable agent opens as a work chat thread
slash-command suggestions in the work chat composer for status, plan, review, terminal, files, and skills
mode selector for direct workspace, isolated worktree, and future remote execution
riskControls: approval and sandbox scope visible before privileged actions
worktree mode required before parallel repository edits

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Claude Desktop makes local MCP capabilities easier to use by managing desktop extensions in settings, surfacing connector status from the chat composer, and making installed tools available in conversations.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Put local tools, MCP servers, and CLI adapters behind one Settings > Capabilities surface, then expose connected capability chips and tool status directly in agent work chats instead of making users edit JSON or type shell bootstrap commands.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 설정에서 로컬 도구를 연결하고, 채팅창에서 어떤 도구가 붙어 있는지 확인한 뒤 바로 작업을 시작한다.
implementationTargets: Settings > Capabilities tab for MCP servers, desktop extensions, and guest CLI adapters
connector chips beside every agent chat composer
one-click install or setup guide for optional local tools
debug log and missing-capability recovery panel
riskControls: sensitive fields use OS secure storage or redacted secret references
enterprise allowlist and disabled connector states are explicit
local MCP beta status and untrusted tool risk are visible before use

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Useful agent products frame work as async tasks with status, follow-up, takeover, validation, branch/workspace isolation, and review.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Represent every launched agent task as a platform-owned run record with workspace, lane, command, output, evidence, validation, handoff, and review status.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 터미널을 직접 붙잡고 있지 않아도 작업 상태와 결과를 앱에서 이어받는다.
riskControls: tool permission prompts for destructive commands
human approval before public workflow side effects

transferPatterns.labelEn: Rules, memory, workflows, and skills are separate
transferPatterns.observedStrength: Users understand configuration better when durable rules, auto memory, manual workflows, reusable skills, and agent definitions are not mixed together.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: The Settings and Agent Core surfaces must make this taxonomy explicit and save each asset into the correct durable path.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 뭘 설정해야 하는지 몰라 헤매지 않고, 반복 작업을 올바른 자산으로 승격한다.
implementationTargets: one settings button with tabs for provider, workspace, rules, memory, workflows, skills, permissions
agent init wizard writes AGENTS.md/rules/skills with preview
riskControls: never write private memories into versioned rules without explicit approval
show activation mode and scope before saving

transferPatterns.observedStrength: The public Claw Code docs frame agent work around slash commands, team-style parallel review, persistent execution loops, skills discovery, config inspection, and CLI bootstrap/init flows.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Expose agent commands, task pipe presets, team/review lanes, skills, and init/doctor/status actions as platform-managed command palette entries instead of hiding them in ad hoc terminal prompts.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 터미널 명령을 외우지 않고, 에이전트 팀 실행과 검증 루프를 앱의 명령/프리셋으로 시작한다.
implementationTargets: command palette entries for init, status, doctor, skills, and team review
task pipe lane for orchestration critique
setup guidance when claw is missing
riskControls: license review required before any bundling

transferPatterns.observedStrength: The Claw Code public docs keep implementation surfaces, command/tool inventories, verification commands, and parity gaps explicit so incomplete ports do not look complete.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Keep every adapter, runtime surface, source editor capability, and generated command family tied to a manifest, parity gap, readiness test, and user-visible capability state.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 실제 구현된 것과 아직 계약/대기 상태인 것을 구분하고, 불완전한 기능을 완성품으로 오해하지 않는다.
implementationTargets: capability parity matrix for each CLI adapter
adapter command inventory in accumulated data
readiness guard for supported adapter list
customer-visible status labels for implemented versus integrated_contract
riskControls: do not mark source-unverified references as copied implementation
validation must prove registry and runtime bridge agree

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Agent tools are safer and easier to trust when pre-tool checks, permission requests, action approval, post-tool logging, and rollback points are visible.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Add a platform permission layer before guest CLI actions and store approval, denial, checkpoint, and rollback records in the runtime data plane.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 파일 수정, 명령 실행, 브라우저 사용, 외부 도구 호출이 앱 안에서 승인되고 되돌릴 수 있다.

transferPatterns.labelKo: 파일 탐색과 코드 편집/디프 리뷰 내장
transferPatterns.labelEn: Embedded file explorer, editor, and diff review
transferPatterns.observedStrength: Developer desktop tools make the file system and proposed changes visible before commit or handoff.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Use the native file workspace and Monaco/source review panes as first-class product surfaces, not a hidden monitoring detail.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 파일시스템을 끌어와 코드와 설정을 직접 보고, 에이전트가 바꾼 내용을 검토한다.
riskControls: customer snapshot strips source file content

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Specialized agents work better when they have narrow prompts, scoped tools, separate context, and clear delegation rules.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Agent Core creates named agents, subagents, skills, tools, prompts, validation gates, and promotion records from repeated human work.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 같은 지시를 반복하지 않고 목적별 에이전트를 쉽게 만들고 개선한다.

transferPatterns.observedStrength: AI coding products gain trust when checks are explicit, repeatable, visible in PR/task lifecycle, and actionable when they fail.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Represent lint, test, config contract, release readiness, customer bundle audit, and hallucination/security checks as run gates with evidence.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 에이전트가 만든 결과가 왜 통과했는지, 어디서 실패했는지, 다음 개선점이 뭔지 본다.
riskControls: no unsupported factual claim without source
record command, exit code, and evidence target

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Good desktop products own install, settings, diagnostics, update, data location, and local runtime boundaries instead of making users run many commands.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: The platform launches first, owns runtime data and UI authority, and invokes guest CLIs or sidecars through explicit adapters.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 명령어를 하나씩 몰라도 앱 설치, 데이터 경로, 진단, 업데이트, 실행을 한 곳에서 관리한다.

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Fast launcher apps reduce friction by making commands searchable, installable, and keyboard-first.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Expose actions such as open workspace, start agent, init rules, run validation, install adapter, and show diagnostics through a desktop command palette.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 메뉴를 찾아다니지 않고 지금 필요한 기능을 검색해서 실행한다.
riskControls: missing adapters show setup guidance instead of blocking the app

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Channel-like organization and decision queues help users separate projects, tasks, handoffs, approvals, and notifications.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Use projects/spaces for work boundaries and a decision inbox for blocked agent questions, permission requests, merge gates, and follow-ups.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 여러 에이전트 작업을 채널처럼 분리하고, 답해야 할 것만 한 곳에서 처리한다.
riskControls: client-side hiding is not treated as security

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Tool ecosystems become safer when scopes, consent, auth, server trust, tool search, and elicitation are visible.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: The platform must manage MCP servers and CLI adapters as capability records with trust level, scope, auth status, and permission prompts.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 에이전트가 어떤 외부 도구와 데이터에 접근하는지 보고 제어한다.

transferPatterns.observedStrength: Agentic systems need design-time controls for indirect prompt injection, excessive agency, external content, secrets, and high-risk tools.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Treat untrusted files/web/docs/logs as data, keep least privilege defaults, require human approval for high-risk actions, and record every exception.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 사용자는 자동화가 편해져도 권한, 외부 입력, 비밀, 위험 명령이 무방비로 실행되지 않는다고 판단할 수 있다.

transferPatterns.labelKo: 사용/평가 데이터 기반 학습 개선 루프
transferPatterns.labelEn: Learning loop from usage and evaluation data
transferPatterns.observedStrength: Users trust agent platforms more when performance, outcomes, memories, decisions, and repeated failures are inspectable and improve future runs.
transferPatterns.platformDecision: Persist task runs, decisions, evidence, work timing, evaluations, intent maps, and promotion candidates so the platform can improve agents and capabilities over time.
transferPatterns.userValueKo: 플랫폼은 작업을 쌓아두기만 하지 않고 반복 병목과 성공 패턴을 기능/에이전트 개선으로 되돌린다.
riskControls: private data stays out of shared memory
AWS AgentCore CLI and credentials remain optional deployment adapters
Lambda or other cloud functions may be remote tool connectors but are not the agent execution host
No AgentCore sample source code is copied into the shipped app
The desktop runtime owns local Python execution, task state, records, and UI authority
Agent proposal records are written through the app-owned native Agent Core command
Provider direct-run and task-run persistence remain the first execution path

checklist: Review src/generated/workspace-snapshot.json before making the repository public.
Remove or redact private notes, secrets, raw prompts, or local-only paths that should not be published.
Regenerate the snapshot after any redaction and run pnpm run build again.
